clinician.final_diagnosis: Concomitant lymph node tuberculosis in a 4-year-old German boy with relapsed ganglioneuroblastoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old German boy with prior stage 4 ganglioneuroblastoma (treated with chemotherapy, MIBG therapy, autologous HSCT, and irradiation) presented with relapse 18 months after initial diagnosis. MRI and MIBG scintigraphy detected new paravertebral lesions, left lower lobe lung lesions, and perihilar lymphadenopathy suspicious for metastases. Biopsy of the paravertebral lesion confirmed ganglioneuroblastoma relapse. Resection of the perihilar lymph nodes revealed noncaseating granulomatous lymphadenitis with epithelioid cells and Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells suspicious for tuberculosis rather than malignant metastases. Immunological testing showed positive interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA), while PCR and mycobacterial cultures were negative. The patient was treated with 2 months of triple anti-tuberculosis therapy (pyrazinamide, rifampin, isoniazid) followed by 3 months of dual therapy (rifampin, isoniazid), concurrent with chemotherapy per the RIST-relapsed Neuroblastoma-2011 protocol. At 3 months post-treatment initiation, MRI demonstrated partial remission of paravertebral lesions and nearly complete remission of lung and lymph node lesions.
